# Sasha Says Rep-Range Choice Depends On Training Phase And Logged Response

Sasha says trainees can choose a rep range based on their current training phase, and he describes a non-exclusive way to lower ranges over time. [src: vid-9yFK1MTYVFE @ 44:42] [src: vid-9yFK1MTYVFE @ 45:40]

## Details
- He says to choose a rep range based on the training phase. [src: vid-9yFK1MTYVFE @ 44:42]
- He says to log training and compare performance to see which ranges work best for the trainee. [src: vid-9yFK1MTYVFE @ 46:15]
- He says the example starts with higher rep ranges and lowers each exercise by one or two reps every month; it is not the only way or the best way. [src: vid-9yFK1MTYVFE @ 45:40]
- He starts the sequence with three times eight. [src: vid-9yFK1MTYVFE @ 45:50]
- The next meso is three times six. [src: vid-9yFK1MTYVFE @ 45:55]
- Then he uses three times four. [src: vid-9yFK1MTYVFE @ 46:00]
- The last meso is four times two; he then mentions rampings with one top set and three back of sets. [src: vid-9yFK1MTYVFE @ 46:03]
- He says trainees can repeat the approach and log performance to learn which rep ranges work best for them. [src: vid-9yFK1MTYVFE @ 46:15]
- He compares a 20-rep dumbbell set approaching failure with two reps at a weight where they can do three reps and says the muscle growth can be the same, depending a little bit on context. [src: vid-9yFK1MTYVFE @ 09:03] [src: vid-9yFK1MTYVFE @ 09:18]

## Evidence
- vid-9yFK1MTYVFE @ 44:42 (Sasha): "my way to go about it go down with the sets maybe two three exactly two to three sets and depending on the phase you're at choose the rep range"
- vid-9yFK1MTYVFE @ 45:40 (Sasha): "A great way to go about it, and it's not the only way and it's not the best way, is you have something that you can actually build over time is you start off with higher rep ranges and every month you go down one rep or two reps for each exercise."
- vid-9yFK1MTYVFE @ 45:50 (Sasha): "So you start with a three times eight"
- vid-9yFK1MTYVFE @ 45:55 (Sasha): "and in the next meso you do a three times six"
- vid-9yFK1MTYVFE @ 46:00 (Sasha): "and then you do a three times four"
- vid-9yFK1MTYVFE @ 46:03 (Sasha): "and in the last meso you do a four times two, for example, and then you do rampings with one top set and three back of sets."
- vid-9yFK1MTYVFE @ 46:15 (Sasha): "You can always repeat it for an infinite amount of time where you will be in certain phases for a certain period of time, see which rep ranges you also perform the best with because you're logging your training and where you perform best and what works for you and what doesn't work for you"
- vid-9yFK1MTYVFE @ 09:03 (Sasha): "if i take 5kg dumbbells i do 20 reps and the last five reps of this 20 rep set i'm actually getting close to failure compared to taking a weight where i can only do three reps and i do two reps of that"
- vid-9yFK1MTYVFE @ 09:18 (Sasha): "you can get the same amount of muscle growth doing both absolutely it will depend a little bit so"
- vid-9yFK1MTYVFE @ 09:22 (Sasha): "let's say you do that set of 20 reps for the bicep whatever and you get to failure obviously so it's gradual you start you have very low degree of effort you're training the fibers but only those fibers that have already grown as much as they can so low threshold fibers"
- vid-9yFK1MTYVFE @ 09:35 (Sasha): "the closer you get to failure the more your effort increases uh the more your brain needs to recruit those muscle fibers that are responsible for moving you know heavier loads or just get recruited because you you're increasing your level of effort"
- vid-9yFK1MTYVFE @ 09:50 (Sasha): "so as you get close to failure you slowly increase that recruitment and at certain point you get to those fibers that can still grow quite a bit right so you can still get to the same outcome"
- vid-9yFK1MTYVFE @ 09:55 (Sasha): "now if you do a set of three which is very heavy you will have this high level of recruitment from the very start"
- vid-9yFK1MTYVFE @ 09:59 (Sasha): "because if you don't have a good level of recruitment the weight will not move it's impossible all of those three reps will be you know very high recruitment many muscle fibers active a lot of mechanical tension in those fibers"
